$comment: Budget breaches accepted in a reviewed change (PRD 9.3). Each entry covers one breach in one load-run record: the budget, the record's commit and the measured value must all match, so a re-run lapses it. The target is never raised; a breach listed here is still a breach. Lapsed entries are removed; their history is in git. See tools/loadrun/accept.ts.

accepted.reason: The same cause as the breach accepted for d1b5c50: one workload question, 'when should an incident be escalated and to whom', gets a complete 563-608-token answer under the served configuration (ADR 0011), and its 20 repeats (7.7% of 260 requests) set the p95 alone. Accepted rather than capped, since shortening the answer would trade completeness for a number. Correction to the earlier acceptance: streaming does not shorten what a user waits for here. PRD 7.2 releases an answer only after verification, so it measures the model's first token (727 ms p95 in this run) without delivering it (ADR 0012).

The retrieval stage runs only on retrieval-cache misses: 13 of 260 requests, so its p95 is the single slowest sample. Nearly all of it is one OpenAI embeddings call. Three misses took 495-564 ms and the other ten 161-298 ms; the two previous runs peaked at 329 and 247 ms, and this commit did not change retrieval code. Read as embedding-API latency varying over a sample too small to have a meaningful p95. Accepted rather than re-run, because re-running until the number fits is not a measurement. What it needs is more cache-miss samples before this budget means anything.
